cleanup_clean_description: Removes JGates objects that are not in use: images of other versions, volumes of workspaces whose folder is gone, stopped containers, run networks, old runs and the old tools folder. Without a scope it cleans all of that; with a scope it cleans only what you name. It lists everything with sizes first and removes nothing without --yes.
cleanup_option_images: Scope: every JGates image that is not in use (they come back with jgates setup).
cleanup_option_workspace: Scope: the volumes and extension images of one workspace id.
cleanup_option_orphans: Scope: the objects of workspaces whose folder no longer exists.
cleanup_option_runs: Scope: only the runs retention (what jgates gc removes).
cleanup_option_legacy_sidecar: Also remove the legacy quality-sidecar image (it has no JGates label, so it is never removed without this flag).
cleanup_option_dry_run: Only lists what would be removed.
cleanup_option_yes: Removes what is listed without asking.
cleanup_bad_workspace_fix: A workspace id looks like ws_ followed by 16 hexadecimal digits (see jgates workspaces).
cleanup_in_use_USED_BY_CONTAINER: a container was made from it
cleanup_in_use_ENGINE: the engine refused: it is in use
cleanup_engine_unavailable: The container engine does not answer: only the data folder is considered.
cleanup_unmanaged_header: Images without a JGates label (never removed unless you say so):
cleanup_unmanaged_hint: Remove the legacy sidecar with jgates clean --legacy-sidecar --yes.
cleanup_summary_dry: {count, plural, one {# object would be removed} other {# objects would be removed}}, freeing about {size}.
cleanup_summary_skipped: {count, plural, one {# object is in use and is skipped} other {# objects are in use and are skipped}}.
cleanup_summary_hint: Nothing was removed. Run again with --yes to remove them.
cleanup_summary_done: {count, plural, one {# object removed} other {# objects removed}}, {size} freed.
cleanup_summary_done_in_use: {count, plural, one {# object was in use and stayed} other {# objects were in use and stayed}}.
cleanup_summary_done_failed: {count, plural, one {# removal failed} other {# removals failed}}.
cleanup_uninstall_description: Removes everything JGates created on this machine: its labelled containers, networks, volumes and images, the old tools folder and the data folder (runs, history, drafts). The key store is removed only after a separate confirmation. Files inside your projects are listed, never touched. Without --yes it only lists.
cleanup_option_uninstall_dry_run: Only lists what would be removed.
cleanup_option_uninstall_yes: Removes what is listed without asking (the key store still needs --include-key-store).
cleanup_option_keep_config_notes: Keep the preferences and the list of known projects in the data folder.
cleanup_option_include_key_store: Also remove the API key store (the semantic-gate secrets file).
cleanup_option_only_workspace: Limit the engine objects to one workspace id (the shared volumes and images stay); used by the acceptance tests.
cleanup_uninstall_home_refused: The data folder was not removed: {reason}
cleanup_home_NOT_A_JGATES_FOLDER: it does not look like a JGates data folder
cleanup_home_TOO_BROAD: it contains your home folder, a drive root or the current folder
cleanup_uninstall_key_store: Key store: {path} (kept; add --include-key-store to remove it)
cleanup_uninstall_key_store_confirm: Also remove the key store {path}? This deletes your saved API keys. [y/N]
cleanup_uninstall_projects_header: Files JGates left in your projects (not touched):
cleanup_uninstall_cli_global: Last step, remove the CLI itself: {command}
cleanup_uninstall_cli_clone: Last step, delete the folder of this clone: {folder}
cleanup_uninstall_summary_dry: Nothing was removed. Run again with --yes to remove everything listed.
cleanup_uninstall_incomplete: Some objects are in use or failed to go; the data folder was kept so you can run this again.
cleanup_uninstall_workspace_scope: Scope: only the engine objects of workspace {id}.
